major_concerns: Simulator (Batfish) mismatch to real hardware may bias measured severity; baseline “LLM-only accept top proposal” is a weak/possibly unrealistic comparator; severity taxonomy and mapping from Batfish outputs to operational high-severity labels is underspecified; repair-loop design may enable degenerate prompt-driven repairs that superficially pass checks.
required_design_repairs: Define and preregister a clear severity taxonomy and exact mapping rules from Batfish outputs to high-severity labels (with examples).
Replace or justify the LLM-only baseline (e.g., top-1 vs top-k, human-reviewed baseline) to reflect realistic acceptance policies.
Predefine exact prompts, seeds, model identifiers, and Batfish configuration; release these artifacts for reproducibility.
Add sensitivity analyses: multiple LLMs or temperature settings and an analysis of repair-loop failure modes (e.g., prompt-gaming).
Preregister stopping/retry rules for repair attempts and how rejected proposals are treated.

major_concerns: Realism of the adversary corpus and poisoning strategies is critical but underdefined; a narrow set of attacks risks overfitting defenses.
Sanitization/provenance defenses may be implementation-specific and brittle; defense evaluation needs adaptive attackers.
RAG stack details (indexing, retriever, chunking) are not fully specified, harming reproducibility.
required_design_repairs: Specify and publish the retrieval pipeline (retriever model, embedding method, index, chunking), the poisoned-document generation process, and the full poisoned KB so experiments are reproducible.
Include multiple attacker strategies (static poisoned docs, rank-manipulation, crafted prompts in retrieved snippets) and at least one adaptive attacker evaluation.
Precisely define provenance-trust scoring and sanitization rules (with thresholds) and preregister them; report false-reject/utility tradeoffs.
Consider evaluating across two retrieval configurations or two LLMs to test generality and avoid overfitting to a single pipeline.

major_concerns: Simulated human-reviewer behavior and latency distributions are central to conclusions but currently rely on deterministic/synthetic rules that may not reflect operational practice.
Non-inferiority margin (+1%) is not justified; results sensitive to this choice.
Throughput modeling assumptions (parallelism, batching, human availability) are underspecified.
required_design_repairs: Ground simulated human reviewer behavior using empirical latency/decision data or clearly justify and preregister the decision rules and latency distributions; publish the simulator code and distributions.
Justify and preregister the non-inferiority margin and run sensitivity analyses across plausible margins.
Clarify operational throughput modeling assumptions (concurrency, queueing) and include alternative realistic scenarios; preregister them.
Report case-level disagreements between validator and human decisions and analyze root causes.

major_concerns: Failure-severity labeling depends on subjective weighting of impacts (affecting correlation target).
Predictive models show association not causation; causal claims must be avoided.
Potential overfitting to curated dataset; external validity unclear.
required_design_repairs: Preregister and publish the severity-weighting methodology (including alternative weightings) and run sensitivity analyses to show robustness of Pearson r to weighting choices.
Emphasize predictive (not causal) framing and add calibration and decision-threshold analyses (sensitivity/specificity) for operational use.
Hold out an external validation set or perform temporal/topology generalization tests to demonstrate robustness; publish feature-extraction code and validator configs for reproducibility.
Include ablation studies to show which validator-derived features drive predictive performance and report uncertainty (bootstrap CIs).
